stem: A grower wants to reduce strong apical dominance and create multiple primary leaders. Which reasoning best supports considering topping rather than assuming the technique will automatically improve production?
choices: Use topping to interrupt apical dominance, then judge the new branching pattern against the canopy goal and plant response
Use topping when higher branch count is desired because removing the apex generally predicts a proportional increase in final yield
Reserve topping for plants that already branch heavily because removing the apex has little influence on apical dominance
Choose topping mainly by the number of cuts that can be made because branch position is less important than cut frequency
rationale: Topping changes apical dominance and subsequent branching, but evidence does not support treating any training method as a universal yield guarantee; the resulting architecture must be judged against the production objective.
